clue.text: Singular Thackeray work seen on TV

indicators.note: making the plural title singular means its final plural letter is dropped

parts.note: The Virginians is a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel turns up, in some odd form, on the television schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' takes the plural S off Thackeray's novel title, leaving the name of the 1960s American TV western.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virginian was a long-running American western series broadcast on television in the 1960s.

parts.note: the Taff is a river in South Wales flowing through Cardiff

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of tea may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something floating in a riverside cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns TEA into ETA. The Taff is the river of Cardiff; the dash in the clue is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and taffeta is a crisp silk fabric.

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: compunction is a feeling of regret or remorse

explanation.surface: A bird appears to feel remorse after being decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the R from REGRET.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white wading heron.

clue.text: One nurse can change disposition, maybe for life

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters that precede it

explanation.surface: A nurse whose temperament might change over a lifetime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NURSE and CAN into NSURANCE, after I for 'One'; 'disposition' means an arrangement, not a temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurance policy is a financial arrangement, or disposition, and life cover is one common kind.

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means the name is written from bottom to top

parts.note: Agag was a king of the Amalekites in the Bible's First Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: A foolish member of an ancient tribe makes an appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses AGAG, a palindrome-like name that reads differently backwards in its vowel order.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga means senile or infatuated and silly, so it matches foolish or fatuous.

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Urals are a mountain range in Russia

explanation.surface: A man named Brown goes mountaineering while jotting things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbs' turns TAN into NAT, as the answer is written downwards. Brown looks like a surname; 'notes' are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, naturals are the signs that cancel a sharp or flat, or the plain notes so marked.

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside another piece

parts.note: ague is a fever, an illness or complaint

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the right to file a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts R inside AGUE; complaint means an illness here, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to dispute or quarrel.

clue.text: Famous U.S. city has West End building

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada

indicators.note: building suggests construction, so these letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: An American city boasts a theatre built in London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' turns END into NED. 'West End' looks like London's theatre district but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone renowned is celebrated and widely known.

clue.text: Poor sot swallows gin perhaps, or this

indicators.note: swallows means one piece is taken inside another
poor here means in bad shape, so the letters of sot are disordered
perhaps signals that the letters of gin may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wretched drunk downs gin or some other drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' makes STO, 'perhaps' makes ING, and 'swallows' sets the second inside the first. 'this' points to the drink the sot might choose instead of gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingo is an old term for strong ale, a drink a sot might take in place of spirits.

clue.text: Object of having a predictor in use on the range

definitions.text: Object of having a predictor in use on the range

parts.words: Object of having a predictor in use on the range
parts.note: having a prophet aims at knowing ahead, while on a rifle range the front sight on the barrel is used for aiming

explanation.surface: A marksman relies on a prediction device at the shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet: the quality of looking ahead, and the front aiming post on a gun barrel used at a range.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the power of anticipating events, and also the front sight of a firearm.

clue.text: Agree to give a hearty welcome

definitions.note: greet as an old noun means a greeting, matching the noun phrase

indicators.note: the words agree to give up the letters sitting across them

explanation.surface: Consenting to receive someone warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'aGREE To'.
explanation.definitionFit: To greet someone is to welcome them, and an old noun use means a salutation.

clue.text: Whole country includes the Northern Territory

indicators.note: includes means the country's name holds another piece inside

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory

explanation.surface: An entire nation stretches to take in an Australian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' places the territory's abbreviation inside the Irish name after its first letter; 'country' does not mean rural land here.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means complete, all of it.

parts.note: frank as a verb means to mark post as free of charge

indicators.note: distribute means spread out, so the letters of won't are reordered

explanation.surface: A man called Frank refuses to hand anything out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribute' rearranges WONT into TOWN; Frank looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Freetown is the capital city of Sierra Leone.

clue.text: Bill has a little money in a manner of speaking

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: An invoice includes a small sum, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a stock phrase, but 'in a' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is a characteristic way of pronouncing words.

explanation.surface: A firm fires its tellers.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them; cashiers are also bank or shop staff handling cash.

parts.note: flaming means burning, on fire
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A bird bursts into flames, out of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is nil in tennis, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a pink wading bird, aptly fiery in colour.

parts.note: the surface suggests a couple marrying, but the naval phrase about splicing a rope means serving a ration of rum

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a couple has married.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Royal Navy, the order to 'splice' a particular rope meant issuing an extra tot of rum, so a pair who got merry had done it.
explanation.definitionFit: The main brace is a ship's rope, and splicing it is the naval idiom for an extra rum issue.

explanation.surface: Asking whether a transaction is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means honest; in poker a straight is a hand of five cards in sequence, dealt to a player.

clue.text: Doesn't agree with vessel entering turbulent northern tides

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes into the middle of another
turbulent means churned up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship's crew object to sailing into rough northern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' makes DIENTS and 'entering' puts the steamship inside it; 'vessel' is the ship, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissent is to disagree with an opinion.

clue.text: Made P C. madly do a bunk

indicators.note: madly means wildly, so the preceding letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A police constable is driven to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' rearranges MADE and PC. 'Do a bunk' is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly.

parts.note: Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A woman named Prudence from the west is drinking a herbal liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: Benedictine looks like the liqueur, but it is a monk, whose title is Dom.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is good judgement, close to prudence.

clue.text: He needs us ? Sounds like it

definitions.text: He needs us ? Sounds like it

parts.words: He needs us ? Sounds like it
parts.note: needs said out loud matches kneads, which is what a person giving massages does to clients

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they are wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is in 'needs', which sounds like 'kneads'.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur is a man who gives massages, working the muscles with his hands.

explanation.surface: A toy for a small Chinese dog.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a chinaman is a left-arm wrist-spin delivery; a native of Peking is, literally, a man of China.

parts.note: the central letter of the word the is the eighth letter of the alphabet, the one people famously fail to sound

explanation.surface: A town centre may be scrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter's name is meant; dropping it is the classic mark of Cockney speech, as in 'ouse' for 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: The written name of the letter H is spelt this way.

clue.text: A helper to Fagin gets less

parts.note: Charley Bates is one of Fagin's boy pickpockets in Dickens's Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: One of Fagin's boys takes a smaller share.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or diminish.

indicators.note: contains means the drawer holds another piece within it

parts.note: a till is a cash drawer
W, west, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: An artist's drawing includes part of a fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' suggests an artist, but it is a cash drawer, TILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ridges.

clue.text: Haven't the heart to go up river

indicators.note: in a down answer going up means the letters are read from the bottom
the heart of a word is its inner letters with the first and last removed

explanation.surface: Lacking the courage to travel upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of HAVENT is AVEN, and 'to go up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neva is the river flowing through St Petersburg.

clue.text: In the team, a rather revolutionary leader

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A team captain who is rather radical.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'teaM A RATher'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was a radical leader of the French Revolution.

indicators.note: repairs means mends or reworks, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone mends the old lining of a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repairs' rearranges AGED and INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a thin, open-weave dress fabric.

explanation.surface: A poem by Oliver Goldsmith, perhaps in a business version.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith wrote the poem with this title; a commercial traveller is a salesman on the road.
